'''Patricia Ann Thiel''' (February 20, 1953 – September 7, 2020) was an American chemist and materials scientist who served as a distinguished professor of [[chemistry]] at [[Iowa State University]]. She was known for her research on atomic-scale structures and processes on solid surfaces.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.chem.iastate.edu/people/patricia-thiel|title=Patricia A Thiel|publisher=Iowa State University, Department of Chemistry|access-date=2019-12-02}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Thiel was raised on a farm in southwest Minnesota, near her birthplace of [[Adrian, Minnesota]]. Her parents grew up in immigrant farm families and each had completed an eighth grade education. Thiel herself attended a private elementary school nearby her farm in [[Lismore, MN|Lismore, Minnesota]], for grades 1-8 and public high school in Adrian, Minnesota for grades 9-12. Support from the [[National Merit Scholarship Program]] enabled her to attend [[Macalester College]] in [[St. Paul, MN|St. Paul, Minnesota]], where she was inspired by her freshman chemistry course and its instructor, Prof. Emil Slowinski <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.startribune.com/obituary-emil-slowinski-wrote-the-book-on-chemistry/341317941/|title=Obituary:Emil Slowinski wrote the book on chemistry|publisher=Star Tribune|access-date=2019-12-02|last= Tim Harlow|date=2015-11-05}}</ref> to major in chemistry. She completed a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in chemistry with a minor in mathematics in 1975, graduating summa cum laude.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Obituary information for Patricia A. Thiel |url=https://www.adamssoderstrum.com/obituaries/obituary-listings?obId=18336909 |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=www.adamssoderstrum.com |language=en-US}}</ref> After working for a year at [[Control Data Corporation]] as an analytic chemist, she enrolled in the chemistry department at the [[California Institute of Technology]], with financial support from a [[National Science Foundation]] Predoctoral Fellowship.  She completed a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in chemistry in 1981 under the supervision of W. Henry Weinberg.<ref name="AVSinterview">{{cite web|url=https://www.avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Awardee-Interviews/Interviews/Pat-Thiel/Interview-Transcript|title=2014 Medard Welch Award - Interview|access-date=2019-12-02|archive-date=2020-08-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200815111350/https://www.avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Awardee-Interviews/Interviews/Pat-Thiel/Interview-Transcript}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mse.iastate.edu/the-department-2/faculty/profile/thiel|title=MSE Faculty and Staff - Patricia Ann Thiel|access-date=2019-12-02}}</ref><ref name="AVSbio">{{cite web|url=https://www.avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Awardee-Interviews/Interviews/Pat-Thiel/Bio|title=Biography: Patricia A. Thiel|publisher=AVS|access-date=2019-12-02|archive-date=2020-09-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924125127/https://www.avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Awardee-Interviews/Interviews/Pat-Thiel/Bio}}</ref>

==Career==
Thiel's first appointment after graduation was as an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]] at [[LMU Munich]], where she worked in the research group of [[Gerhard Ertl]], who later went on to receive the 2007 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]]. In 1982, she joined the technical staff of [[Sandia National Laboratories]] in [[Livermore, CA|Livermore, California]], and, after a brief stint as a [[visiting professor]] in the physics department of the [[University of California, Berkeley]], joined the chemistry department faculty of [[Iowa State University]] in 1983, with a simultaneous appointment as staff scientist with the US Department of Energy's [[Ames Laboratory]]<ref name="AVSbio"/>. She was subsequently promoted to the ranks of [[Associate Professor|associate professor]] (1988), [[Full Professor|full professor]] (1991) and [[Distinguished Professor|distinguished professor]] (2001). She received an additional appointment as professor of materials science and engineering in 2012. During her time at Iowa State, Thiel was a supervisor for the thesis research of around thirty PhD students and ten Master's students.<ref name=":0" /> Throughout this time period she received outstanding teaching awards,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.las.iastate.edu/2013/09/04/winter-thiel-receive-cassling-family-faculty-awards-for-outstanding-teaching/|title=Winter, Thiel receive Cassling Family Faculty Awards for outstanding teaching|access-date=2020-01-01|archive-date=2021-01-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210117192619/https://archive.las.iastate.edu/2013/09/04/winter-thiel-receive-cassling-family-faculty-awards-for-outstanding-teaching/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and held several administrative posts, including program director for materials chemistry (Ames Laboratory; 1988–2004), chief research officer (Ames Laboratory; 2008–2009) and chair of the Iowa State Chemistry Department (1999-2002). Thiel was an associate editor of ''[[The Journal of Chemical Physics]]'' (2013–2020).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aip.scitation.org/jcp/info/editors|title=The Journal of Chemical Physics - Editorial Board|access-date=2019-12-02|website=The Journal of Chemical Physics}}</ref> She attended the [[Nobel Prize]] ceremony on December 10, 2011, where [[Dan Shechtman]] received the 2011 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery of [[quasicrystal]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ameslab.gov/news/pat-thiel-talks-about-attending-nobel-prize-ceremony|title=Pat Thiel talks about attending the Nobel Prize ceremony|access-date=2019-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150804043227/https://www.ameslab.gov/news/pat-thiel-talks-about-attending-nobel-prize-ceremony|archive-date=2015-08-04}}</ref> In 2019, Theil was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-04-17 |title=Ames Laboratory scientist Patricia Thiel elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences {{!}} Ames Laboratory |url=https://www.ameslab.gov/news/ames-laboratory-scientist-patricia-thiel-elected-american-academy-arts-and-sciences |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=www.ameslab.gov |language=en}}</ref>



==Research==
Thiel's research elucidated [[Atomic spacing|atomic-scale]] structures and processes on solid surfaces, in areas relevant to [[microelectronics]], [[tribology]], [[heterogeneous catalysis]], and [[nanoscience]]. She published over 300 research papers, which have been cited about 12,000 times, effective 2019. She is especially known for work in the following three areas.

===Surfaces of quasicrystals===
Thiel's research group pioneered studies of nucleation and growth of metal films on [[quasicrystal]] surfaces, demonstrating that local [[pseudomorph]]ic growth, including [[starfish]]-shaped formations, can occur at very specific nucleation sites.<ref>{{ Cite journal|last1=Cai|first1=T.|last2=Ledieu|first2=J.|last3=McGrath|first3=R.|last4=Fournée|first4=V.|last5=Lograsso|first5=T.A.|last6=Ross|first6=A|last7=Thiel|first7=P. A.|title=Pseudomorphic starfish: Nucleation of extrinsic metal atoms on a quasicrystalline substrate|journal=Surf. Sci.|volume=526|issue=1–2|pages=115–120|year=2003|doi=10.1016/S0039-6028(02)02593-1|bibcode=2003SurSc.526..115C}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sharma|first1=H.R.|last2=Shimoda|first2=M.|last3=Tsai|first3=A.P.|year=2007|title=Quasicrystal surfaces:structure and growth of atomic overlayers|journal = Advances in Physics|language=en|volume=53|issue=3|pages=403–464|doi=10.1080/00018730701269773|bibcode=2007AdPhy..56..403S|s2cid=120873116}}</ref>
Focusing on metallic, aluminum-rich quasicrystals, Thiel and her collaborators extensively explored how quasicrystal atomic-scale surface structures were related to their unusual surface properties, including low friction, low adhesion, and good oxidation resistance.<ref>{{Cite journal|first1=J. Y.|last1=Park|first2=D. F.|last2=Ogletree|first3=M.|last3=Salmeron|first4=R. A.|last4=Ribeiro|first5=P. C.|last5=Canfield|first6=C. J.|last6=Jenks|author6-link=Cynthia Jenks|first7=P. A.|last7=Thiel|title=High frictional anisotropy of periodic and aperiodic directions on a quasicrystal surface|journal=Science|volume=309|issue=5739|pages=1354–1356|year=2005|doi=10.1126/science.1113239|pmid=16123295|bibcode=2005Sci...309.1354P|s2cid=20967375|url=http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/23c0/23c6bc3fb9ed98d6b32b02ff65efbfcb3b96.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200316025110/http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/23c0/23c6bc3fb9ed98d6b32b02ff65efbfcb3b96.pdf|archive-date=2020-03-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Macia|first=Enrique|year=2006|title=The role of aperiodic order in science and technology|journal=Reports on Progress in Physics|language=en|volume=69|issue=2|pages=397–441|doi=10.1088/0034-4885/69/2/R03|bibcode=2006RPPh...69..397M|s2cid=120125675 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=McGrath|first1=R.|last2=Ledieu|first2=J.|last3=Cox|first3=E. J.|last4=Diehl|first4=R. D.|author4-link=Renee Diehl|year=2002|title=Quasicrystal surfaces: structure and potential as templates|journal=J. Phys.: Condens. Matter|language=en|volume=14|issue=4|pages=R119–R144|doi=10.1088/0953-8984/14/4/201|s2cid=250871398 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Krim|first=J.|author-link= Jacqueline Krim |year=2012|title=Friction and energy dissipation mechanisms in adsorbed molecules and molecularly thin films|journal = Advances in Physics|language=en|volume=61|issue=3|pages=155–323|doi=10.1080/00018732.2012.706401|bibcode=2012AdPhy..61..155K|s2cid=218647448}}</ref>

===Interaction of water with metal surfaces===
Thiel's Ph.D. research described evidence for [[hydrogen bond]]ing between water molecules on a ruthenium surface. She continued her research on water as a faculty member at Iowa State University, and discovered that desorption kinetics of water can exhibit a measurable [[isotope]] effect.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Thiel|first1=P. A.|last2=Hoffmann|first2=F. M.|last3=Weinberg|first3=W. H.|title=Monolayer and multilayer adsorption of water on Ru(001)|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=75|issue=11|year=1981|pages=5556–5572|issn=0021-9606|doi=10.1063/1.441960|bibcode=1981JChPh..75.5556T}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Doering|first1=Dale.L.|last2=Madey|first2=Theodore E.|year=2002|title=The adsorption of water on clean and oxygen-dosed Ru(001)|journal = Surface Science|language=en|volume=123|issue=2–3|pages=305–337|doi=10.1016/0039-6028(82)90331-4}}</ref> She was credited with being the first to propose that bilayers of water near solid surfaces could possess a structure similar to the basal plane of [[Ice Ih]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Henderson|first=Michael A.|year=2002|title=The interaction of water with solid surfaces: fundamental aspects revisted|journal = Surface Science Reports|language=en|volume=46|issue=1–8|pages=1–308|doi=10.1016/S0167-5729(01)00020-6|bibcode=2002SurSR..46....1H}}</ref> 
She was the co-author, along with [[Theodore E. Madey]], of a highly cited and comprehensive review article describing the interactions and properties of water near solid surfaces.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Thiel|first1=Patricia A.|last2=Madey|first2=Theodore E.|title=The interaction of water with solid surfaces: Fundamental aspects|journal=Surface Science Reports|volume=7|issue=6–8|year=1987|pages=211–385|issn=0167-5729|doi=10.1016/0167-5729(87)90001-X|bibcode=1987SurSR...7..211T}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hodgson|first1=A.|last2=Haq|first2=S.|year=2009|title=Water adsorption and the wetting of metal surfaces|journal = Surface Science Reports|language=en|volume=64|issue=9|pages=381–451|doi=10.1016/j.surfrep.2009.07.001|bibcode=2009SurSR..64..381H}}</ref>

===Nucleation, growth, and coarsening of metal nanostructures on surfaces===

Thiel's group was credited with discovering that large two-dimensional islands of metal [[adatom]] clusters can have significant room temperature mobility on metal substrates,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ala-Nissila|first1=T.|last2=Ferrando|first2=R.|last3=Ying|first3=S.C.|title=Collective and single particle diffusion on surfaces|journal=Advances in Physics|volume=51|issue=3|year=2002|pages=949–1078|doi=10.1080/00018730110107902|bibcode=2002AdPhy..51..949A|s2cid=103078504}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=Zhenyu|last2=Lagally|first2=Max G.|title=Atomistic processes in the Early Stages of Thin-Film Growth|journal=Science|volume=276|issue=5311|year=1997|pages=377–383|doi=10.1126/science.276.5311.377|pmid=9103189}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Wen|first1=J. -M.|last2=Chang|first2=S. -L.|last3=Burnett|first3=J. W.|last4=Evans|first4=J. W.|last5=Thiel|first5=P. A.|title=Diffusion of Large Two-Dimensional Ag Clusters on Ag(100)|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=73|issue=19|year=1994|pages=2591–2594|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.2591|pmid=10057099|bibcode=1994PhRvL..73.2591W|url=https://lib.dr.iastate.edu/chem_pubs/78}}</ref> and that, contrary to what had usually been assumed, this can be the main route to coarsening (an evolution to larger sizes and fewer numbers) of these clusters.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jensen|first1=Pablo|title=Growth of nanostructure by cluster deposition: Experiments and simple models|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=71|issue=5|year=1999|pages=1695–1736|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.71.1695|arxiv=cond-mat/9903141|bibcode=1999RvMP...71.1695J|s2cid=119440413 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Wen|first1=J.-M.|last2=Evans|first2=J. W.|last3=Bartelt|first3=M. C.|last4=Burnett|first4=J. W.|last5=Thiel|first5=P. A.|title=Coarsening Mechanisms in a Metal Film: From Cluster Diffusion to Vacancy Ripening|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=76|issue=4|year=1996|pages=652–655|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.652|pmid=10061513|bibcode=1996PhRvL..76..652W|url=https://lib.dr.iastate.edu/chem_pubs/79}}</ref> She and James W. Evans are responsible for first describing an atomic-scale mechanism for metal film growth, which they dubbed 'downward funneling'.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Evans|first1=J. W.|last2=Sanders|first2=D. E.|last3=Thiel|first3=P. A.|last4=DePristo|first4=Andrew E.|title=Low-temperature epitaxial growth of thin metal films|journal=Physical Review B|volume=41|issue=8|year=1990|pages=5410–5413|issn=0163-1829|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.41.5410|pmid=9994410|bibcode=1990PhRvB..41.5410E|url=https://dr.lib.iastate.edu/bitstreams/30fd2dc1-e995-49a4-a6d5-85658a9b87bc/download}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Lapujoulade|first1=Jean|title=The roughening of metal surfaces|journal=Surface Science Reports|volume=20|year=1994|pages=191–249|issue=4|doi=10.1016/0167-5729(94)90004-3|bibcode=1994SurSR..20..195L}}</ref> Because of this mechanism, they predicted an unusual variation in film roughness with temperature from theory, and eventually confirmed it experimentally using [[scanning tunneling microscopy]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Stoldt|first1=C. R.|last2=Caspersen|first2=K. J.|last3=Bartelt|first3=M. C.|last4=Jenks|first4=C. J.|author4-link=Cynthia Jenks|last5=Evans|first5=J. W.|last6=Thiel|first6=P. A.|title=Using Temperature to Tune Film Roughness: Nonintuitive Behavior in a Simple System|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=85|issue=4|year=2000|pages=800–803|issn=0031-9007|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.800|pmid=10991402|bibcode=2000PhRvL..85..800S|url=https://dr.lib.iastate.edu/bitstreams/74b69598-fc26-47ff-9292-3670e69b23f1/download|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Voter|first1=Arthur F.|last2=Montalenti|first2=Francesco|last3=Germann|first3=Timothy C.|title=Extending the Time Scale in Atomistic Simulation of Materials|journal=Annu. Rev. Mater. Res.|volume=32|pages=321–346|year=2002|doi=10.1146/annurev.matsci.32.112601.141541}}</ref> This is now accepted as an important mechanism that affects thin film morphology upon growth at low temperature.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Evans|first1=J.W.|last2=Thiel|first2=P.A.|last3=Bartelt|first3=M.C.|title=Morphological evolution during epitaxial thin film growth: Formation of 2D islands and 3D mounds|journal=Surface Science Reports|volume=61|issue=1–2|year=2006|pages=1–128|issn=0167-5729|doi=10.1016/j.surfrep.2005.08.004|bibcode=2006SurSR..61....1E}}</ref>

More recently, her group discovered a series of naturally occurring metal-sulfur complexes with distinct [[Stoichiometry|stoichiometries]], which may influence stability of larger metallic features by assisting surface metal transport and hence coarsening. Adamson Award for Distinguished Service in the Advancement of Surface Chemistry|access-date=2019-12-02|website=Chemical & Engineering News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ameslab.gov/node/8357|title=Thiel Selected for ACS Adamson Award for Surface Chemistry|access-date=2019-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150805024712/https://www.ameslab.gov/node/8357|archive-date=2015-08-05|website=Ames Laboratory}}</ref>
* 2010 [[David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics]], "For seminal contributions to surface structure and dynamics of complex metallic alloys, including quasicrystals and kinetically limited growth and relaxation of nanostructures in thin metal films."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/adler.cfm|title=David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics|access-date=2019-12-02|website=American Physical Society}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Thiel&first_nm=Patricia&year=2010|title=2010 David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics Recipient|access-date=2019-12-02|website=American Physical Society}}</ref>
* 2010 Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],"For increasing the level of understanding of surface properties of metallic quasicrystals, and for work on pathways by which metallic nanoclusters and thin films form and rearrange on metal surfaces."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.news.iastate.edu/news/2011/jan/AAASfellows|title=AAAS honors Iowa State, Ames Lab researchers for distinguished science|access-date=2020-08-22|archive-date=2019-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621062444/https://www.news.iastate.edu/news/2011/jan/AAASfellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> 
* 2011 John D. Corbett Professor in Chemistry<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ameslab.gov/node/9080|title=Pat Thiel Named to Corbett Professorship|access-date=2019-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150804042039/https://www.ameslab.gov/node/9080|archive-date=2015-08-04|website=Ames Laboratory}}</ref>
* 2012 Fellow of the [[Materials Research Society|Materials Research Society (MRS)]], "For seminal contributions to understanding the structure, reactivity, and tribology of quasicrystal surfaces, and to understanding growth and stability of metal nanostructures and metal thin films."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.advancedsciencenews.com/materials-research-society-announces-2012-mrs-fellows/|title=Materials Research Society Announces 2012 MRS Fellows|access-date=2020-03-16|last=Dave Flanagan|website=Advanced Science News|date=19 March 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mrs.org/mrs-fellows-2012|title=2012 MRS Fellows|access-date=2019-12-02|website=Materials Research Society|archive-date=2019-07-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708150508/https://www.mrs.org/mrs-fellows-2012}}</ref>
* 2014 [[Physical Review]] Journals - Outstanding Referee<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.aps.org/OutstandingReferees|title=Outstanding Referees Program|access-date=2019-12-02|website=American Physical Society}}</ref>
* 2014 [[Medard W. Welch Award]], "For seminal contributions to the understanding of quasicrystal surfaces and thin-film nucleation and growth."<ref name="AVSinterview"/>
* 2019 Elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news.iastate.edu/news/2019/04/16/patthiel|title=Patricia Thiel of Iowa State, Ames Laboratory elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=2019-12-02|website=Iowa State University of Science and Technology|date=April 16, 2019|archive-date=2020-10-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201006230527/https://www.news.iastate.edu/news/2019/04/16/patthiel|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Thiel was born on February 20, 1953, in Adrian, Minnesota. She married James William Evans, an Australian-born physicist, in 1988. They have two daughters, both engineers.<ref name="AVSinterview" />
Thiel died of undetected breast cancer on September 7, 2020, at her home surrounded by her husband and daughters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adamssoderstrum.com/obituaries/Patricia-A-Thiel?obId=18336909|title=Patricia A. Thiel Obituary|access-date=2020-09-21}}</ref>
